div.div:
لَوْجَاءُ and ↓ لُوَيْجَاءُ [the latter the dim. of the former] A want; a thing wanted; an object of want: (TA:) from لَاجَهُ as explained above. (K.) ―
-b2- مَا فِى صَدْرِهِ حَوْجَآءُ وَلَا لَوْجآءُ إِلَّا قَضَيْتُهَا There was not a want in his bosom but I accomplished it. (TA.) ―
-b3- مَالِى فِيهِ حَوْجَآءُ وَلَا ↓ لَوْجَآءُ وَلَا حُوَيْجَآءُ وَلَا لُوَيْجَآءُ I have no want, [nor any little want,] with respect to him, or it. (Lh.) ―
-b4- مَالِى عَلَيْهِ حِوَجٌ وَلَا لِوجٌ [I have no wants which it is incumbent upon him to supply: حَوَجٌ being a pl. of حَاجَةٌ; and لِوَجٌ, irregularly, of لَوْجَآءُ, in imitation of حِوَجٌ]. (TA.) ―
-b5- See also حَوْجَآءُ, in three places.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
